notes: Structure: all 11 sections present and in correct order for every task. TDD Anchor present on all (all are code tasks). No template placeholders ([Task Name], {PK path}, {reviewer-name}) and no TODO/FIXME/TBD markers remain in body content.

Frontmatter: status=planned everywhere (correct for iteration 1); depends_on arrays valid; wave numbers >= 1; skills=[code-writing] arrays; reviewers arrays of 3; verify field correct vs tech-spec (Task 1/3/5 = [] with no Verify-smoke in tech-spec; Task 2/4 = [smoke] matching tech-spec Verify-smoke). teammate_name empty/optional — ok.
Reviewer report paths correctly anchored to work/11-funnels-interactive/logs/working/task-N/ (not bare logs/).
Consistency: frontmatter.skills == Required Skills section; frontmatter.reviewers == Reviewers section for all tasks. code-writing -> code-reviewer+test-reviewer (+security-auditor) satisfied.

Decomposition: dependency graph valid and acyclic. Task 3 (wave 2) depends_on [1,2] (wave 1); Task 4 (wave 2) depends_on [1]; Task 5 (wave 3) depends_on [3] (wave 2). Every dependency references an existing lower-wave task. No cycles, no missing dependency declarations.

Traceability: each task's Files-to-modify matches the corresponding tech-spec Implementation Tasks entry (Task 1/2/3/4/5). Task 1 legitimately extends to engine/trigger/service files for additive $in edits and documents the rationale in Details.

Shared Resources (tech-spec Architecture): all 4 resources (TelegramSender, Clock, EventService, JobRunr sweep) are pre-existing singletons reused, not newly created. No owner-task needed; consumers (Task 3/5) correctly depend on the producing Wave-1 tasks. No competing instances in same wave.
Carry-forward: tech-spec has a single global Acceptance Criteria section (no per-task AC/TDD blocks). Per-task descriptions and AC are faithfully expanded into each task with no scope dropped.

Atomicity: each task is a single cohesive unit (Task 1 = model+status foundation; Task 2 = sender; Task 3 = engine; Task 4 = validation+DTO; Task 5 = callback wiring). No merge or split candidates; no over-decomposition.
